uncertainty_notes: Traced FIX-26 lastActiveDate gating (spend>0 only), FIX-13 strict-> tie policy, FIX-06 second-pass budget normalization, and #IN-02 chronologically-latest budget/effectiveStatus selection. All four invariants hold under same-date duplicates, null-then-non-null sequences, out-of-order date arrivals (backfills), and mode='campaign' vs mode='adset'. The seed/update coordination (lines 84-110 seed + 111-167 update on the SAME first row) correctly does not double-count because (a) numeric accumulators are seeded to 0 before the += on line 112-116, and (b) every budget/status update guards `r.date > prev` where prev was just set to r.date by the seed, evaluating false. storeFilter being matched by display name (line 76) is an explicit deferred-refactor documented inline (IN-07); not flagged. Lexicographic string date comparison on line 67/124/138 etc. relies on ISO YYYY-MM-DD format from the upstream CampaignRow contract; safe today.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No direct regression for effectiveStatus latest-date selection and duplicate-date tie policy.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: The off-chip in CampaignsTableRow depends on aggregate().effectiveStatus; same-day duplicate rows with ACTIVE/PAUSED could silently change which UI status renders if the strict-> tie policy drifts. The seed-then-update coordination is particularly subtle (line 104 seeds unconditionally, line 109 only sets the date tracker if truthy, line 161 only updates if truthy).
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Two rows for one campaign on the same date with effectiveStatus ACTIVE then PAUSED (assert first-write 'ACTIVE' wins). Add an older non-null status (PAUSED, 2026-05-10) and a newer null status (2026-05-15) and assert the non-null PAUSED survives (late-arriving NULL must not clobber per line 161 gating).

test_coverage_gaps.description: No direct coverage for a latest-date row whose campaignBudgetCad is null while an earlier row's value is non-null.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: aggregate() intentionally keeps the latest-NON-NULL budget (lines 136-142 gate on `r.campaignBudgetCad != null`). A newer null value must NOT clobber an older non-null. Without this regression the gating could be relaxed accidentally to `r.campaignBudgetCad !== undefined` (which would let null overwrite), silently flipping budget displays to '—' for currently-active campaigns whose latest backfilled row had a null budget cell.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Older CBO row with campaignBudgetCad 50 at 2026-05-10, newer CBO row with campaignBudgetCad null at 2026-05-15. Assert row.campaignBudgetCad === 50. Mirror for ABO adSetBudgetCad.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No coverage for storeFilter being a display name versus storeId.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Line 76 filters by r.storeName, not r.storeId. Current STORE_TAB_CONFIG keeps display names unique ('uzoshop', 'Zol Plus', '360usmile') so the contract works today. If a caller passes 'zolplus' (the id) the filter silently returns zero rows. The IN-07 inline comment documents this as a deferred refactor; a contract-pinning test makes the regression visible the day STORE_TAB_CONFIG grows a duplicate name.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Rows with storeId 'zolplus' and storeName 'Zol Plus'. Assert aggregate(rows, 'campaign', 'Zol Plus', 'all', range) returns the rows and aggregate(rows, 'campaign', 'zolplus', 'all', range) returns [].

test_coverage_gaps.description: No coverage for empty/missing adSetId in adset mode.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Line 82 constructs the adset key as `${storeId}::${platform}::${campaignId}::${adSetId}`. Google campaign-level fallback rows and any malformed source rows with adSetId='' would collapse to the same key suffix, causing distinct conceptual rows to aggregate together. CampaignRow.adSetId is typed as plain `string` (no `| undefined`), so the empty-string case is real.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Two distinct rows in adset mode with the same storeId/platform/campaignId but blank adSetId, differing campaignName or spend. Assert and document the expected grouping behavior (currently: a single row collapsing both).

test_coverage_gaps.description: No coverage for the date-range filter on line 67 (out-of-range rows excluded).
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Lexicographic comparison `r.date < range.from || r.date > range.to` is only safe for ISO YYYY-MM-DD. A regression that lets pre-range or post-range rows slip in would silently inflate spend/conversion totals for the selected window.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Rows on 2026-04-30, 2026-05-01, 2026-05-31, 2026-06-01 with the same key. Range {from:'2026-05-01', to:'2026-05-31'}. Assert aggregated spend equals exactly the sum of rows on 05-01 and 05-31.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No coverage for budgetType='' (unknown) preserving both campaignBudgetCad and adSetBudgetCad through the FIX-06 second pass.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: The FIX-06 normalization on lines 172-175 only clears budgets when budgetType is 'CBO' or 'ABO'. If budgetType resolves to '' (paused / lifetime-only / Google), both budget fields are emitted as-is — possibly with mixed-source values. Pinning this prevents a future 'normalize to null on unknown' refactor from silently dropping the visible budgets.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Single row with budgetType='', campaignBudgetCad 50, adSetBudgetCad 25. Assert both survive in the output unchanged.
